newsitem.title: BELGIUM: NATO said wanting new warcrimes police in Bosnia. [CORRECTED 12:22 GMT]
newsitem.headline: NATO said wanting new warcrimes police in Bosnia. [CORRECTED 12:22 GMT]

text.p: NATO defence ministers have reached broad agreement in principle that a new international police force is needed in Bosnia to capture indicted war criminals, a senior U.S. defence official said on Wednesday.

"There is broad agreement in principle to do this. There isn't yet a specific plan on how to march forward," the offical said after U.S. Defence Secretary William Perry held talks with French Defence Minister Charles Million and then with the defence ministers of Norway, the Netherlands (Corrects from Finland) and Denmark on Wednesday.

The official, who asked not to be identified, told reporters the police force could operate directly under the U.N. criminal tribunal for former Yugoslavia, which is based in the Hague, or under the auspices of the European Union or the Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe (OSCE).
"What they (defence ministers) are looking for now is what you would call it, who would run it, how it would be organised, who would contribute to it," the official said.

The official stressed that ministers had agreed that a new 30,000-member military stabilisation force (SFOR) being sent to Bosnia this month to replace the current peacekeeping force should not be asked to arrest indicted war criminals. But SFOR could work closely with the police force, he said.

The official said there was deep concern among ministers that only seven out of about 80 suspected war criminals had been captured in the past year and that those indicted should be captured and tried under the Dayton peace accords.
